answer: Attention-history ledger. Each identity must accumulate a public trail of solved micro-tasks whose difficulty adapts to prior accuracy; the ledger acts as a mirror of sustained effort, not wealth. Registration alone yields nothing—spending appears only after consistent correct work. An attacker cloning identities must independently redo every task, paying wall-clock time and compute per clone, while a single identity's history cannot be copied without detection via pigment-tagged task variants. Cheap sybils stall at zero reputation; the marginal comet of new identities costs full task replay.
